observation: The 2995-case Class-A run passed and its artifact validated, but promotion then exposed two exact BK-24-AC1 references absent from the canonical population. Both tests existed and ran in the ordinary-local stage; that is not the bound Class-A evidence the acceptance registry requires. Backlog lint correctly refused both claims.
repair: Classify the two existing offline scripted integration/adversarial witnesses as Class-A. Assertions, fixtures, production code, test bodies and authority are unchanged. The ordinary selector excludes Class-A, so this moves two cases between disjoint local populations instead of duplicating their execution. It does not authorize real acquisition or external requests.

verification.limits: Test bodies and production code unchanged. No live acquisition or full packet acceptance claim.

lesson: Check claimed automatic acceptance references against the selected population before an expensive run; function existence alone cannot establish membership. The previous valid Class-A artifact was not sufficient to validate every authored acceptance claim.
